title: Staged TTL annealing with shadow canaries and key-family-aware bucketing
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Summary: Build an automated, auditable pipeline to suggest and safely apply prefix/KV TTL changes using a staged annealing approach. We will (1) compute robust per-key-family hit-rate models from production traces, (2) propose TTL deltas that optimize marginal cost-per-served-token subject to latency SLOs, (3) validate proposals via replayed shadow canaries, and (4) perform conservative progressive applies with automatic rollback triggers.

Background & Motivation: Current TTL tuning is either manual heuristics or coarse global policies. That leads to suboptimal cost tradeoffs across mixed workloads where a small number of prefix families dominate cost. We need a system that: learns empirical decay patterns, translates them into safe configuration deltas, and can apply changes with strong safety gates.

Novel technical approach:
- Key-family bucketing: classify prefixes into key families by stable attributes (route, model, customer tier, shape signature). Maintain per-family reservoirs for statistics rather than per-prefix only, reducing noise for sparse prefixes.
- Survival/hazard modeling: use a hybrid Kaplan–Meier + Weibull fit to estimate the tail decay of hit probability across time-since-last-access. This gives an empirical survival curve for each key family rather than assuming exponential TTL decay.
- Marginal-cost gradient: compute the estimated cost delta per token served when TTL changes (+/-) by small factors using simulated batching and hit/miss replays. Rank candidate changes by marginal savings per 1% risk of added miss latency.
- Annealing schedule generator: produce staged TTL multipliers (e.g., 0.8 -> 0.9 -> 1.1 -> 1.2) with explicit confidence bands and applied percentiles to limit blast radius.
- Shadow canary harness: apply proposed TTLs to a shadow cache layer during live traffic replay (no customer-facing effect) for 24–72 hours across representative traffic slices. Collect p50/p95/p99 latency, miss-rate, cost-per-token, and burst behaviour statistics.
- Safe apply orchestration: a progressive apply engine that (a) starts at 1% traffic, (b) increases to 5%/20%/100% when safety predicates are met, and (c) automatically reverts when triggers breach thresholds.

Deliverables:
- Scoring engine that emits TTL proposals with reasoning and confidence band for each key family.
- Simulator that replays 7d production traces and synthetic surge scenarios to estimate worst-case behavior.
- Shadow-canary infra + dashboards to collect safety signals.
- Orchestration playbook and automated rollback mechanism wired to routing and config APIs.

Risks and mitigations:
- Sparse families: bucketing reduces variance; for extremely rare prefixes fall back to conservative global defaults.
- Correlated load spikes: include surge augmentation in replay scenarios and require additional safety steps for families with high burstiness.
- Measurement bias from sampling: use stratified reservoir sampling and validate against full-scan backfill runs for a subset.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field below.
acceptance_criteria: Scoring engine produces TTL proposals for >=90% of requests by volume across top 200 families.
Simulator can replay 7 days of production traffic and produce reproducible delta estimates for hit_rate/latency/cost.
Shadow canary run for two representative families demonstrates <5% change in p95 latency and cost reduction >=3% for accepted proposals.
Orchestration can perform staged apply (1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%) and auto-revert on defined triggers within 5 minutes.
Runbook and dashboard for manual override + post-apply summary are available and linked from the PRD.
testing_plan: Unit tests for the survival/hazard estimator and marginal-cost calculator (target >90% branch coverage).
Offline replay tests: deterministic replays with seeded RNG using anonymized 7d traces. Compare baseline vs candidate TTLs.
Chaos tests: run replay with synthetic bursts (2x, 5x, 10x) to validate worst-case thresholds.
Shadow canary: run proposals in shadow mode on 3 different time windows, collect metrics for at least 48h each.
Preflight PR: include a canary run dashboard screenshot and simulation outputs before merge.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal low-volume families, shadow only (24-72h).
Phase 1: 1% traffic apply for families that pass shadow checks (48h).
Phase 2: 5% traffic apply (24h), require p95/p99 delta within thresholds to proceed.
Phase 4: 100% apply if all predicates hold for 72h. Immediate automated rollback otherwise.
Manual escalation: pager duty to runtime team if auto-revert occurs or if p99 latency increases >20% for >10m.
monitoring: Metrics to monitor: miss_rate_by_family, cache_byte_hit_rate, tokens_served_per_prefix, p50/p95/p99 latency by family, request_tail_latency, model_throughput, per-model cost-per-token.
Safety predicates: absolute p99 delta <= +10ms AND relative p99 delta <= +10% AND miss_rate relative change <= 2x baseline.
Alerting rules: page on p99 delta > +20% for >5m OR miss_rate absolute increase >3% for >10m OR cost increase >5% for >30m.
Dashboard: TTL proposal view with survival curves, simulated savings, shadow run summary, staged-apply timeline.
